summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal bloating and changes in gastrostomy tube output, including increased volume and brown or green-yellow discoloration. She has a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, and prior C. difficile. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV antibiotics (initially Zosyn, then transitioned to Ceftriaxone and Flagyl). A KUB showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern, and a contrast G-tube study confirmed proper placement and patency. Soap enemas were used to relieve distention. By hospital day 2, symptoms improved, she tolerated a bariatric stage 5 diet, and tube feeds were planned for restart at home. She remained afebrile with normal labs and was discharged home on oral Flagyl with follow-up instructions.
